item.description: - Codex sessions now show in their workspaces as working or idle, with the project, how long, and a notification when a long turn finishes. They count in the menu bar, the island, the jump shortcut and `dashbar status`. Dashbar reads only the folder and when each turn starts and ends, never your messages. Codex doesn't record when it's waiting for you, so a session asking for approval still reads as working. - Claude's weekly Fable limit now shows with your other plan limits, when your account has one. - Extra usage now shows what you've spent of your monthly cap, such as "£10.80 of £40.00", beside the percentage.

- Going back to a session now opens the session itself, not just its app: in Orca, that session's workspace; in T3 Code, its thread; in the Claude app, its Code conversation. Click a session, a notification or the island, or press the jump shortcut. If an app doesn't take the link, it still comes forward as before. - Workspaces get a button for the app their agent runs in, such as Orca, T3 Code or the Claude app, beside the editor and terminal ones. In the panel's Now card it shows when the card has more than one session; with one, clicking the session does the same. - Sessions in Orca's terminal panes are now recognised as Orca's. Before, clicking one did nothing useful. - Small polish on the action tiles: the icons read as one size, and a session's hover highlight has room around its text.

- Weekly plan limits now show today's share: what was left at midnight, spread over the days until the reset, so you can see how much you can use today and still last the week. On the Usage tab the bar draws today's use lighter, with a tick where today's share ends, and the line under it reads like "Today 6% of about 21%". The History page says the same under each weekly chart. 5-hour limits are unchanged. - A new notification, off by default (Settings → Notifications → Today's share of weekly limits), tells you once a day when a weekly limit has used today's share, so you can ease off early. Going on is fine; tomorrow's share is just smaller. - `dashbar status` adds today's share to weekly limits, and `dashbar status --json` has `todayShare` and `usedToday` for them. The dashbar-status skill tells agents to mention it before heavy work.
